title: GradReason: LLMs as Meta-Learners that Replace Training Epochs with Training-Data-Free Weight Updates

headline_result.text: Over 12 runs, Claude Opus 5.5 used 32.8% fewer data epochs than the 80-epoch recipe at 0.31 points lower test accuracy, but a fixed snapshot-averaging rule without an LLM saved 25.0% and could not be told apart from Opus.

limitations_stated.text: Snapshot averaging is a known technique (SWA, LAWA) published before the models' training cut-offs; the LLM selected rather than invented it.
limitations_stated.quote: This finding has a limit. Snapshot averaging was not new.

limitations_stated.text: The evaluation is small: three small architectures, two 32x32 datasets, two seeds per setting and two LLMs from one provider.

notes_for_review: An LLM agent reads weight snapshots and epoch gradients every ten epochs and writes programs that replace some training epochs with gradient-free weight updates. The careful design includes budget-matched recipe baselines, a frontier comparison and two fixed-rule controls; the result is that the LLM rediscovered snapshot averaging (SWA/LAWA-like), and a fixed rule encoding it matches Opus within the resolution of 12 runs. This is a clear case where the LLM's contribution reduces to selecting a known mechanical update; wall-clock cost exceeded savings, and code/transcripts are promised only upon publication.
